archetypes.name: parser-sibling-consistency
archetypes.rationale: The plan replaces three ${2:?...} expansions with explicit larch_err/exit-2 guards, relying on claimed sibling-flag patterns in write-run-params.sh that must be verified before the diff is trusted.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that --review-budget and --workflow-path in write-run-params.sh actually use the explicit [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2-}" ]] + larch_err + exit 2 pattern the plan uses as a model, not a different shape. Check that --partition-requested and --brainstorm-requested currently use ${2:?...} as the plan claims, so the proposed mirror-change is not targeting code that already differs. Confirm the plan's proposed if-block structure matches the existing argument-parser style (shift 2, fall-through, flag name in error string) so the diff does not introduce inconsistency with adjacent cases. Identify any other multi-word flags in write-run-params.sh that use ${2:?...} but are NOT listed for update, which would leave the parser in a mixed rejection-path state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: pin-string-accuracy
archetypes.rationale: The stale-prose absent checks and grep-Fq jq-filter pin embed literal strings that must match actual file content exactly, or the lint is a no-op or fails on day one.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the eight absent-check phrases ('no auto-apply', 'user is always prompted', 'Gate B always prompts', 'fail-closed to manual') do NOT currently appear in approval-gates.md or SKILL.md — if they do, the plan's claim that these are stale-only patterns is wrong and the new lint would fail immediately on the existing corpus. Confirm that the full jq-filter string the plan proposes to pin is an exact substring of the SKILL.md Step 0b block, including pipe separators, spacing, and variable names, not a paraphrase that would make grep -Fq return nonzero. Verify the plan's claimed existing-pin line numbers (396 for brainstorm arm, 506 for manual_gate_b) are accurate in the current test-design-structure.sh, so the rationale for not duplicating those pins is sound. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-guard-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The new harness reproduces the SKILL.md Step 0b outer guard and jq-merge inline; drift between the harness and SKILL.md makes the test validate the wrong behavior without CI catching it until the structural pin fires.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the recovery_merge_if_needed() function in the proposed harness exactly replicates the SKILL.md Step 0b outer guard condition, including the command -v jq availability check and the specific boolean-OR trigger clause — a guard that is too loose or too strict would let assertions pass even when SKILL.md's recovery path is unreachable or always-triggered. Verify that case 2's assertion (manual_gate_b == false and partition_requested == true) is the correct expected output under SKILL.md Step 0b semantics when manual argv is false and partition argv is true, not an accidental inversion of the OR-merge versus overwrite semantics. Confirm the plan's decision to omit an all-false-argv no-op case is deliberate and documented, since that path exercises the guard-entry condition directly and its absence is a coverage gap claim the plan does not address. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
